200.title: Former Polish defence minister opposes transfer of Patriot missiles to Ukraine
200.summary: Mariusz Błaszczak, former Polish defence minister, has said that the government's plans to provide Ukraine with missiles for Patriot air defence systems are unacceptable.
200.body: Mariusz Błaszczak, former Polish defence minister, has said that the government's plans to provide Ukraine with missiles for Patriot air defence systems are unacceptable. Source: Błaszczak on X (Twitter), as reported by European Pravda Details: The former minister was responding to comments by Deputy Defence Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who said that a decision on providing Ukraine with missiles for Patriot systems could be made in the coming days. Following the latest incident in which a missile fell on Polish territory, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that Warsaw will shortly consider transferring additional missiles for Patriot air defence systems to Ukraine. Ukraine is suffering from an acute shortage of missiles for Patriot systems – the only air defence systems capable of intercepting Russian ballistic missiles.

200.body: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers Aug 14, 2026 | Business , Energy & Climate , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. 300.title: Inflation eases apart from Poland and Czechia
300.summary: Apart from Czechia and Poland, inflation have declined further in July. In Romania, we expect to see dynamic disinflation in the second half of the year with headline inflation falling toward 5.9% at the end of the year.Market movementsRomanian central bank will consider lowering interest rates after the inflation rate drops below the benchmark rate, according to Governor Isarescu.
300.body: Apart from Czechia and Poland, inflation have declined further in July. The government's decision to end measures that had been mitigating retail fuel price increases where behind the acceleration of inflation in Poland to 3% y/y in July from June’s 2.5% y/y (13.9% m/m increase in fuel prices) Food prices continued to decline marking the third consecutive monthly drop, but the decrease was not sufficient to offset the impact of higher fuel prices. The other countries worth mentioning are Hungary (inflation at 1.2% y/y sets the path for further monetary easing) and Romania, where inflation eased to 8.2% y/y. In Romania, we expect to see dynamic disinflation in the second half of the year with headline inflation falling toward 5.9% at the end of the year.Market movementsRomanian central bank will consider lowering interest rates after the inflation rate drops below the benchmark rate, according to Governor Isarescu.

600.body: Polish football club GKS Katowice could be hit with tough Uefa sanctions after footage of their fans appearing to make Nazi salutes towards Israeli supporters emerged on social media. A crowd of just under 12,500 attended the match, but a video posted on X showed several fans, wearing the Polish club's distinctive black and yellow colours, making what appeared to be fascist gestures as they left. According to one report, during the first half, home fans unfurled a large banner reading "RED IS BAD", a reference to Hapoel's reputation as a left-wing club. The spokesperson added: “Where matters are reported, proceedings are opened and should they lead to disciplinary sanctions being imposed, they are announced on the UEFA disciplinary website.” Last month UEFA fined Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia more than £40,000 after its fans were found to have made Nazi salutes and were guilty of “violent conduct” at a Europa League game against Derry City in Northern Ireland.
